title: Dynamics of cool flames
summary: Review of cool-flame dynamics: low-temperature chemistry, cool flames in microchannels, microgravity droplet combustion, counterflow and turbulent flames, flammability diagrams of low-temperature flames.

items.claim: Review covering microgravity droplet cool flames and counterflow cool flames (the PSI-142 motivation).
items.quote: Next, the recent experimental and computational findings of cool flames in microchannels, microgravity droplet combustion, counterflow flames, and turbulent combustion environments are reviewed.

notes: Abstract via Semantic Scholar; accepted manuscript on ScienceDirect refused automated access.

title: The radical index and the effect of oxygen concentration on non-premixed cool flame extinction of large n-alkanes
summary: Counterflow cool-flame extinction of n-heptane to n-dodecane at several fuel and O2 fractions (fuel side 550 K, oxidiser 300 or 550 K, atmospheric). Cool-flame reactivity scales as [O2]^n; the measured n = 1.7 is above the n = 1.5 derived from the ISS droplet experiments, and the authors call the results consistent with those droplet extinction data. Kinetic models over-predict n-heptane cool-flame extinction strain rates by at least a factor of two. A cool-flame radical index rises with chain length.

items.claim: Measured oxygen exponent n = 1.7 for cool-flame reactivity, larger than n = 1.5 derived from the ISS (FLEX) n-alkane droplet extinctions; results judged consistent with the droplet measurements.
items.quote: In this study, we measured n = 1.7, which is greater than n = 1.5 derived from the microgravity droplet experiment.

items.claim: Consistency with microgravity droplet extinction data.
items.quote: The results are consistent with the measurements of extinction conditions in microgravity n-alkane-droplet experiments [27,29].
the cool flame low temperature reactivity of n-alkanes is proportional to nth power of oxygen mole fraction, [O2]n, with n = 1.5-2.

items.claim: All kinetic models used over-predict n-heptane cool-flame extinction strain rates by at least a factor of two.
items.quote: all of the employed kinetic models over-predict the cool flame extinction strain rates for n-heptane by at least a factor of two

items.claim: Test conditions: fuel-side burner 550 K, oxidiser side 550 or 300 K, atmospheric counterflow, 22.5 mm nozzle separation.
items.quote: The upper/fuel-side burner temperature (Tf) is maintained at 550 ± 5 K, and the bottom/oxidizer-side burner temperature is maintained at 550 ± 5 K or 300 ± 5 K.

notes: Accepted manuscript on OSTI (purl 1865795, Elsevier user licence). Acknowledges NASA grant NNX16AK07G. The n = 1.7 vs 1.5 link to FLEX was added to the record.

title: Study of the low-temperature reactivity of large n-alkanes through cool diffusion flame extinction
summary: Hot and cool counterflow diffusion-flame extinction of n-heptane to n-tetradecane: similar hot flames, larger n-alkanes far more reactive as cool flames, ozone nearly suppresses the difference, and models over-predict cool-flame extinction limits. Already in the record.

items.claim: Larger n-alkanes more reactive in the cool-flame regime; ozone suppresses differences.
items.quote: It is observed that while these fuels behave similarly for hot flames, the larger n-alkanes are substantially more reactive in the low-temperature cool flame regime.
a general overprediction of the measured cool flame extinction limit is observed for all of the fuels studied

notes: Abstract from the Princeton research portal (as in the record); ScienceDirect accepted manuscript refused automated access.

title: Counterflow flame experiments and chemical kinetic modeling of dimethyl ether/methane mixtures
summary: Counterflow hot, cool and ozone-assisted cool flames of DME/methane blends: methane raises hot-flame but lowers cool-flame extinction limits; the original model over-predicts cool-flame extinction, fixed by updating DME + OH and other reactions.

items.claim: Model over-prediction fixed by updating DME + OH H-abstraction.
items.quote: The measurements indicate that the original kinetic model significantly overpredicts the cool flame extinction limits.

title: Low-temperature multistage warm diffusion flames
summary: Experimental evidence of self-sustaining multistage warm diffusion flames (dibutyl ether) between cool and hot flames at 1 atm; ozone strengthens the second stage; hot flames can extinguish into warm or cool flames. Authors note relevance to microgravity because of long residence times.

items.claim: Warm flame as bridge between cool and hot flames.
items.quote: Hence, the results suggest that the multistage warm flame can act as a critical bridge between cool flames and hot flames

items.claim: Authors flag warm flames as particularly relevant to microgravity (long residence times).
items.quote: The multistage warm diffusion flame is particularly relevant to combustion in highly turbulent flow fields and in microgravity environments, owing to the possibility of long residence times.

notes: Abstract via Semantic Scholar. The fuel is dibutyl ether (abstract), resolving the record's gap on data ID 5's fuel only if ID 5 is this paper's data.

title: Dynamics and burning limits of near-limit hot, warm, and cool diffusion flames of dimethyl ether at elevated pressures
summary: Computed DME counterflow flame regimes at elevated pressure and temperature with and without radiation: hot, warm and cool flames, epsilon-shaped flammability diagram, cool flames by radiative or stretch extinction. Already in the record.

items.claim: Cool flame formed by radiative or stretch extinction; epsilon-shaped diagram.
items.quote: It is also shown that the cool flame can be formed in several different ways: by either radiative extinction or stretch extinction of a hot flame or by stretch extinction of a warm flame.

title: On the chemical characteristics and dynamics of n-alkane low-temperature multistage diffusion flames
summary: First experimental demonstration of n-alkane (n-heptane, n-decane, n-dodecane) multistage diffusion flames at 1 atm; near extinction dynamics controlled by the first (peroxy) stage; ozone doping reveals a separate low-temperature ozone-assisted mode.

items.claim: Near extinction, multistage dynamics controlled by the first (peroxy) stage.
items.quote: Moreover, near extinction where the flame temperature is low, the multistage flame dynamics are controlled by the first oxidation stage, governed by peroxy chemistry

title: Pressure and Radiation Effects on the Dynamics of Hot and Cool Diffusion Flames
summary: ICDERS 2017 extended abstract (computations, DME): pressure-weighted strain scaling holds for hot but not cool flames; at elevated pressure N2 dilution of the oxidiser shifts hot-flame extinction strongly and enables a steady 'mild flame' branch, made more stable by radiation. Motivated by ISS droplet cool flames.

items.claim: Cool flames do not scale with pressure-weighted strain.
items.quote: It is seen that the similarities in hot flames at constant pressure-weighted strain rate do not extend to cool flames due to changes in the nature of low-temperature chemistry across different pressures.

items.claim: At elevated pressure, N2 dilution of the oxidiser enables a steady 'mild flame' branch sustained by intermediate-temperature chemistry; radiation stabilises it further (computational).
items.quote: At elevated pressures, N2 diluent addition to the oxidizer is shown to shift the extinction limits of the hot flame dramatically and enables the formation of a steady “mild flame” branch

notes: No DOI. Free PDF on icders.org (link given by Semantic Scholar). Computational conference paper; the 'mild flame' result is a precursor of the warm-flame work and was not added as a separate record finding.

title: Transient interactions between a premixed double flame and a vortex
summary: Premixed DME/O2/O3 double flames near the hot-flame extinction limit interacting with a vortex: local extinction leaves a lone cool flame; extinguished hole, cool flame and double flame can coexist; curvature matters.

items.claim: Vortex extinguishes near-limit hot flame leaving a lone cool flame.
items.quote: It is seen that the vortex can extinguish the near-limit hot flame locally, resulting in a lone cool flame.
